sources.name: Municipality of Idrija — Mercury heritage nomination
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: Primary nomination dossier reviewed September 2026. Printed pages 246, 255, 264, 308 distinguish discovery, mining, the 1977 suspension and the last extraction in 1994. UNESCO representative old-town/mining-landscape coordinate, not an individual shaft.

periods.description: Approximate eleventh-century start of the documented mining tradition. Closure on 30 June 1988 is recorded by the mine museum: https://blog.rammelsberg.de/2018/07/30-juni-1988-30-juni-2018-30-jahre-betriebsende-am-rammelsberg/. No undated zinc co-production is backdated.
UNESCO documents extraction since the thirteenth century; 1201 is a century-level boundary, not an exact opening. AGH geological research distinguishes the 1996 end here from Bochnia’s 1990 closure.
Polish Geological Institute history: mine established with its shaft in 1251 and production ended in 1990. The 1248 discovery is not used as extraction.

Prefectural heritage record documents silver mining from 1526 and 32 working pits in the 1823 inventory. This is a district-level historical phase; 1823 is the last dated inventory used here, not a claimed closure.

The official record explicitly dates the reopening to 1887 and the end to 1923. Silver continued alongside copper. The unreviewed 1824–1886 interval remains empty rather than implying uninterrupted extraction.
The documented Roman mining phase, from the Dacian conquest to the Roman withdrawal. Later medieval and modern phases are not joined across the evidence gap.

sites.name: St Just — historic copper and tin mining district

periods.description: Coverage of the industrial mining landscape’s documented 1700–1914 period. Approximate district marker for multiple workings; these limits are not the opening and closure of every constituent mine.

sites.name: Camborne and Redruth — historic copper and tin mining district

periods.description: Coverage of the industrial mining landscape’s documented 1700–1914 period. Approximate district marker for multiple workings; these limits are not the opening and closure of every constituent mine.

UNESCO records at least 1,200 years of operation ending in 1962. The approximate lower bound is 1962 minus 1,200 years, not an exact foundation date. Brine extraction at Salins; the distant Arc-et-Senans processing works are not a second deposit.

Natural History Museum Vienna archaeological chronology: developed Bronze Age mining from approximately 1500 BCE; the latest dated wooden finds are from 1245 BCE. Later Bronze Age extraction is not attested here. Astronomical year numbering.

Iron Age mining documented from around 800 BCE (https://www.nhm-wien.ac.at/hallstatt/en/site/hallstatt_period) until the destructive event around 350 BCE. The intervening archaeological gap remains empty.

The historic operator places the mining tradition in the third century BCE; the approximate lower boundary is 300 BCE. University of Murcia research distinguishes extraction ending in 2001 from metallurgy ending in 2003. Long mining-tradition interval; intermediate interruptions are not resolved.

sites.name: Tarnowskie Góry lead, silver and zinc mining district

periods.description: Municipal World Heritage history identifies the first principal phase around 1490–1600, extracting argentiferous lead. Sporadic later workings are not filled in.
Documented second phase of deeper industrial extraction at the Fryderyk mine.
The same history explicitly attests zinc production in the nineteenth century; it is not retroactively assigned to the medieval phase. Century-level coverage, not exact commodity start/stop dates.

sites.name: Cerro Rico de Potosí — silver mining district

periods.description: Mining began in 1545 (https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/883/). UNESCO describes continuing mining after its nineteenth-century decline and the 2005 technical mission. This mining-tradition interval ends at a dated attestation, not an asserted closure; interruptions and individual workings are not resolved.
Nomination p.246 distinguishes discovery in 1490 from mining dated to 1497 by Valvasor. Temporary suspension decided early in 1977 (p.308); intra-year detail is unavailable at atlas year resolution.
Production resumed in 1984 (p.251). Mining ended in 1994, while mercury processing lasted until 1995 (p.255). The full 1978–1983 gap and the later processing-only years are excluded.

audit.scope: Individually sourced historical extraction phases. Representative districts are named as such. Archaeological and century-level dates are approximate. No deposit occurrence is turned into an operating interval.
audit.coordinates: UNESCO component coordinates are used where available. Hallstatt uses the CC0 Wikidata cultural-landscape representative coordinate. Potosí uses USGS major-deposits record 889.
audit.excluded: Arc-et-Senans is a processing site supplied with brine from Salins and is not counted as another extraction site.
